description: Boundary pressure declines while social foundations and rights-based institutions strengthen.
Technology and markets reduce carbon intensity but material and land pressures remain.
Delayed structural reform increases dependence on future technology and risk management.
Protection becomes uneven while cooperation weakens and ecological pressure remains high.
Extraction and fossil dependence continue until cascading crises force reactive measures.
Regional restoration and resilience reduce pressure but global coordination remains uneven.
International cooperation strengthens around climate biodiversity oceans chemicals finance and standards.
Adaptation becomes unequal and boundary pressure remains high as vulnerable groups absorb losses.
